## Dependence on our biggest customer

Baylor Foods (party:887387e1) is our largest customer, at **37.85%** of invoiced revenue in the trailing 12 months (2025-09-29 to 2026-09-29), per the `customer_concentration` metric. That is roughly 6.6x the size of our next four largest customers, each of which sits at 5.74% of revenue. This is a heavy concentration: over a third of the business runs through one account.

## Do they pay on time? No.

Looking at open (unpaid) invoices for Baylor Foods (all-time, `invoice.state = open`):
- Total open: **$75,547.04** across 16 invoices
- None current, none 1-30 days, none 31-60 days
- **$37,773.52** sits in the 61-90 day overdue bucket
- **$37,773.52** sits in the 90+ day overdue bucket (past our internal escalation threshold)

Their DSO (days sales outstanding) is **78.6 days**, versus **57.8 days** company-wide, a clear laggard.

Put in company context: total open receivables firm-wide are $146,622.60, and Baylor Foods alone accounts for over half of that ($75,547.04, ~51.5%). More strikingly, Baylor Foods holds $37,773.52 of the company's total $38,956.34 in invoices over 90 days overdue, essentially the entire book of severely late receivables sits with this one customer.

## Policy note
Per the collections policy, the 61-90 day Baylor invoices are still eligible for a standard reminder email. The 90+ day invoices, however, are past the 90-day cutoff and must be escalated to the owner rather than emailed a routine reminder. I did not send anything or propose a hold since none was requested; if you want, I can draft the owner escalation for the 90+ bucket or propose reminder emails for the 61-90 bucket.

ANSWER: Baylor Foods is our largest customer at 37.85% of trailing-12-month revenue (vs 5.74% for each of the next four), and they are a slow, currently-overdue payer: all $75,547.04 of their open invoices are past due, split evenly between the 61-90 day bucket and the 90+ day bucket, and their DSO (78.6 days) runs well above the company average (57.8 days). Baylor alone holds over half of the firm's total open receivables and nearly all of its 90+ day overdue balance, so this is both a concentration risk and a collections risk in the same account.
